:::{.callout-important}

A mean proportional to exposure, $\E{Y_t} = \rate t$,
has no term that stays nonzero at $t = 0$:
a model of this form says that with no exposure, no events are expected.
A mean with an added constant, such as $\E{Y_t} = c + \rate t$ with $c > 0$,
would expect $c$ events even with no exposure.
Regression models for counts keep the proportional form when they add covariates
(see [rme's count-regression chapter](https://morrison-lab.github.io/rme/chapters/count-regression.html)).

:::
